subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 7-year-old girl is evaluated for fatigue and easy bruising. Laboratory studies show pancytopenia with a hypocellular bone marrow. Examination reveals absent thumbs, a hypoplastic radius, and several cafe-au-lait spots. Chromosomal analysis after exposure to a DNA cross-linking agent shows markedly increased chromosome breakage.
question: Which of the following DNA repair processes is most likely impaired in this patient?

options.text: Homologous recombination-mediated repair of DNA interstrand crosslinks

explanation_correct: Fanconi anemia results from defects in the Fanconi anemia pathway that repairs DNA interstrand crosslinks, with homologous recombination acting downstream to restore the duplex. Cells are hypersensitive to cross-linking agents, and patients develop pancytopenia, skeletal anomalies such as absent thumbs, cafe-au-lait spots, and cancer predisposition.

explanation_incorrect.A: Nucleotide excision repair removes bulky helix-distorting adducts but not interstrand crosslinks.
explanation_incorrect.B: Mismatch repair corrects mismatched nucleotides in newly synthesized DNA.
explanation_incorrect.C: Base excision repair removes small altered bases such as deaminated cytosine.
explanation_incorrect.E: Proofreading removes misincorporated nucleotides during replication; it is not the defect in Fanconi anemia.

educationalObjective: Fanconi anemia reflects defective repair of DNA interstrand crosslinks through the Fanconi anemia/homologous recombination pathway.
